source.book: Tajweed Rules of the Qur'an — Part One
source.verification: book source checked; Qur'anic references cross-checked

prerequisites: Identify izhar, both idgham groups, and iqlab.
learningOutcomes: Define ikhfa' as a pronunciation between izhar and idgham.
Identify ikhfa' within one word and across two words.
Keep a two-count ghunnah while preparing for the following letter.
Classify ikhfa' correctly in at least 8 of 10 mixed examples.

technical.ar: الإخفاء الحقيقي هو النطق بالنون الساكنة أو التنوين بحالة بين الإظهار والإدغام، من غير تشديد، مع بقاء الغنة مقدار حركتين، إذا جاء بعدها أحد حروف الإخفاء الخمسة عشر.
technical.en: Ikhfa' is pronouncing noon saakinah or tanween in a state between clear pronunciation and merging, without a shaddah, while maintaining a two-count ghunnah before one of its fifteen letters.

studentFriendly.ar: لا نظهر النون كاملة ولا ندمجها بالكامل؛ نخفي صوتها مع غنة حركتين ونهيئ الفم للحرف التالي.
studentFriendly.en: Do not make noon fully clear and do not merge it completely. Conceal it with a two-count ghunnah while preparing for the next letter.

definition.memoryFormula: نْ أو تنوين + ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك = إخفاء بغنة حركتين

teacherPreparation: Prepare fifteen trigger cards in three groups of five.
Keep the excluded groups visible: throat letters, idgham letters, and ba.
Model clear noon, merged noon, and concealed noon as a three-way contrast.
Correct tongue preparation according to the following letter through live listening.

openingReview.teacherPrompt: Name the six idgham letters and ba for iqlab.
Explain what remains when the noon is concealed.

conceptExplanation.text: After removing the six izhar letters, six idgham letters, and ba, the remaining fifteen letters cause ikhfa'. The noon is concealed with two-count ghunnah.
Teach the fifteen letters in manageable groups, then move quickly to mixed decisions. The following letter influences oral preparation and the quality heard in practice.

lessonPath.title: Exclude
lessonPath.text: Remove izhar, idgham, and iqlab letters.

lessonPath.title: Prepare
lessonPath.text: Move the mouth toward the next letter.

visualExplanation.display: نْ / ً ٍ ٌ + ت ث ج د ذ ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ف ق ك ← إخفاء + غنة حركتين
visualExplanation.teacherUse: Reveal the letters as three groups of five.

ruleSummary.condition: Noon saakinah or tanween is followed by one of the fifteen ikhfa' letters.
ruleSummary.result: Conceal the noon between izhar and idgham with two-count ghunnah.
ruleSummary.location: It can occur within one word or across two words.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Conceal noon with two-count ghunnah while preparing for ta.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ta follows noon saakinah across two words.
quranExamples.commonError: Touching the full noon articulation point and making it too clear.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Conceal noon with two-count ghunnah before shin.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Shin is one of the fifteen letters.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Conceal noon inside the word and prepare the lower lip for fa.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Fa follows noon saakinah within one word.
quranExamples.commonError: Thinking ikhfa' occurs only across words.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Conceal noon with two counts while preparing for the heavy sad.
quranExamples.commonError: Making the ghunnah too light before the heavy following letter.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Conceal noon with two counts while preparing for heavy qaf.
quranExamples.commonError: Changing noon to mim as though qaf were ba.

guidedPractice.studentAction: Exclude known groups, then name ikhfa'.
guidedPractice.feedback: Require the trigger letter and two-count ghunnah.

guidedPractice.teacherAction: Model clear, merged, then concealed versions.
guidedPractice.studentAction: Identify the correct middle state and imitate it.
guidedPractice.feedback: Correct clarity, merging, timing, and next-letter preparation separately.

interactiveActivities.prompt: Choose the first group of five.
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. This is the first group.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The first five are ت ث ج د ذ.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. This is the second group.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The second group is ز س ش ص ض.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. All fifteen are now complete.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The final group is ط ظ ف ق ك.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Noon is concealed, not fully clear or fully merged.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ikhfa' is the middle state between clarity and merging.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Shin is an ikhfa' letter.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Inspect the first letter after noon.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Fa triggers ikhfa' inside the word.
Correct. Qaf is the trigger, not the later ba.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Use only the letter immediately after noon.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Shin belongs to the fifteen.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Compare shin with the four rule groups.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Ba is reserved for iqlab.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ba is not one of the fifteen ikhfa' letters.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Ayn is a throat letter.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ayn belongs to the six izhar letters.

instruction.en: A learner makes noon fully clear before shin. What should change?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Stay between clarity and merging.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ikhfa' requires the middle concealed state.

instruction.en: A learner changes noon to mim before qaf. Which rule did they confuse it with?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Only ba changes noon to hidden mim.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The hidden mim belongs specifically to ba.

items: Between izhar and idgham with two-count ghunnah
acceptedAnswers: Between izhar and idgham with two-count ghunnah
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. This is the complete practical definition.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Include both the middle state and ghunnah timing.

instruction.en: How many ikhfa' letters are there?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. You are ready for mixed review.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Add the three groups of five.

commonMistakes: Merging noon completely into the next letter.
Changing noon to mim when the trigger is not ba.
Looking at a later letter instead of the immediate next letter.
Using one identical mouth position for all fifteen letters.
correctionTechniques: Use a three-way contrast: izhar, ikhfa', idgham.
Keep the four rule groups visible during early decisions.
Practice three letter groups before all fifteen together.
Correct ghunnah timing and next-letter preparation separately.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Name all fifteen letters in three groups.

knowledgeChecks.success: At least eight are correct with reasons.

teacherQuestions: What is the immediate next letter?
Does it belong to izhar, idgham, iqlab, or ikhfa'?
Is noon fully clear, fully merged, changed, or concealed?
How do you prepare for the next letter?
studentTasks: Classify mixed examples from all four rules.
Recite examples with varied following letters.
independentPractice: Write the fifteen letters in three groups.
homework: Prepare five ikhfa' examples using different trigger groups.
For each: identify the trigger, explain the rule, then recite.
exitTicket: Name the fifteen letters in groups.
Recite one selected example with two-count ghunnah.
masteryCriteria: Distinguishes ikhfa' from the other three rules.
Identifies at least 8 of 10 mixed items.
Avoids full clarity and full merging.
teacherNotes: This lesson needs repeated listening across more than one session.
Letter-list mastery is not equivalent to recitation mastery.
Keep the learner focused on the immediate next letter.
Use mixed review before moving to written tanween changes.
sourceNotes: The rule and fifteen-letter set use page 47.
Grouping, activities, and teaching sequence are curriculum-design additions.
